4) Retention defaults: what are default retention windows for logs, request traces, and billing records? Can these be shortened (or set to 0) per contract?

Olivia —

Appreciate the clear list. High-level answers below; looping in Neha (Security) and Karthik (Dedicated product) for the technical appendix and attestation.

- Region pinning: Yes — Dedicated pools can be anchored to a single cloud region. Customer data and runtime replicas are constrained to that region unless you explicitly request multi-region DR.

- Isolation: Dedicated uses tenant-dedicated GPU hosts with network isolation via private endpoints/VPC connectivity. No cross-tenant containers or host sharing in the dedicated pool.

- Deletion & erasure: We have a deletion playbook: mark-for-deletion -> revoke access + schedule crypto-key rotation -> zero/overwrite ephemeral disks -> purge backups per retention policy. I will let Neha/Karthik list timings and control IDs.

- Retention defaults: default traces/billing logs are 30 days; audit logs retained 365 days by default. These are contractually configurable.

Next steps: Neha/Karthik — can you provide a short technical appendix that (a) states exact timelines for crypto-erase and VM image purge, (b) confirms that snapshots/backups remain in-region by default, and (c) gives guidance on how we can shorten retention windows per-customer? If you can produce a one-page attestation we can route to Olivia's legal team.

Thanks —
Marcus
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

Hi Olivia/Marcus —

Following up with the security/compliance specifics you asked for. Below is a concise technical appendix you can include in your binder. Happy to redline language for an SOW or attestation.

Technical appendix (security highlights):
- Region locality: Dedicated pools are deployed into customer-chosen region (e.g., us-west-2). Control RWI-12 ensures that production persistent volumes, object storage snapshots, and scheduled backups are kept within the selected region by default. Cross-region replication only occurs when configured for explicit DR/replication purposes and requires customer opt-in.

- Isolation: Tenancy is tenant-dedicated; we do not colocate tenant workloads with other customers on the same GPU hosts in Dedicated. Network endpoints are private (no public ingress). All inter-service traffic within the pool traverses private subnets.

- Encryption & key management: Per-tenant encryption-at-rest using customer-managed keys (CMKs) via your KMS is supported. Key rotation and access revocation are audited.

- Deletion flow and timelines:
  * Initiation: Customer requests deletion via Console or API (immediate).
  * Mark-for-delete: Orchestration marks objects and metadata; access is revoked (T+0).
  * Crypto-erase: We schedule KMS key destruction/ciphertext revocation where customer-managed keys are used — crypto-erase completes within 24 hours of key destruction confirmation. For Redwood-managed keys, crypto-erase is completed within 72 hours.
  * Ephemeral scrub: Background scrub job zeroes ephemeral disks and clears KV caches; scrub completes within 24–72 hours depending on instance lifecycle.
  * Snapshot/backups: Snapshots are soft-deleted and then purged per retention window: default snapshot purge is 30 days unless contract specifies otherwise. Snapshots do not leave the pinned region unless cross-region DR is enabled.

- Logs & traces retention: Default request trace retention = 30 days (configurable to a minimum of 0 days by contract). Billing records are retained for invoicing (90 days minimum by default); audit logs retained 365 days. We can alter these windows in the contract (addendum required).

- Evidence & controls: See SOC2 summary for control mappings; we can provide a signed attestation for region-locality and deletion timelines. Internal playbook: https://redwood-drive.company.com/teams/security/dedicated-region-playbook

If you need the text in a particular legal phrasing for Procurement, send a template and we'll fill it in.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor

Olivia —

Adding the operational/engineering perspective and specific mechanics for Dedicated pools. Short answers first, details below.

Short: nodes and storage are region-anchored; replication is limited to that region unless DR is requested. Deletion is a multi-step orchestration that includes immediate access revocation, KV cache TTL enforcement, zeroing ephemeral storage, and KMS-backed crypto-erase; full purge of VM artifacts completes within 72 hours in typical workflows.

Details:
- Placement & anchoring: We use cloud placement groups + affinity rules so dedicated GPU hosts are physically launched in the selected region’s AZs only. The orchestration layer enforces region affinity for any autoscaled instances attached to the pool.

- Storage surface: Persistent volumes for customer data live in region-local block/object stores. We do not replicate persistent volumes to other regions by default. Backups (snapshots) are stored as region-scoped objects; cross-region copy must be enabled explicitly.

- KV caches & prefix caching: Runtime caches (KV caches for model context) are ephemeral and bound to nodes in the pool. They are not written to persistent object storage by default. Cache eviction and TTL are configurable; for high-security customers we recommend TTL=0 and prefix caching disabled.

- Deletion orchestration steps (more precise):
  1) API/Console delete -> mark-for-delete record created (T+0)
  2) Immediate ACL revoke and revocation of temporary tokens (T+0)
  3) Background scrub of ephemeral disks & in-memory caches (T+0 to T+72h)
  4) Snapshot lifecycle: soft-delete + purge (default purge 30d)
  5) KMS key retirement and ciphertext invalidation -> crypto-erase considered effective at key destruction time (T+24h for CMK-managed, T+72h for Redwood-managed keys)
  6) Final VM image and metadata purge from control plane (T+72h).

- Auditability: All steps generate audit events with timestamps and job IDs; audit logs are stored in-region and available for export.

- Contract options: We can commit to shorter crypto-erase windows, immediate snapshot purge, and minimum trace retention = 0 as contract options for an enterprise SOW. These options will be listed in the Dedicated SOW addendum.
